definition: Credit-claiming occurs when a senator (or a release written on the senator’s behalf) presents the senator as personally responsible for, or substantially responsible for, producing a positive governmental outcome or achievement. The outcome may be tangible (funding, grants, projects, disaster declarations, facilities, benefits, appointments secured) or legislative (passage, approval, adoption, inclusion, or implementation of a bill, amendment, provision, or policy change). The key element is that the senator claims or receives credit for bringing about the outcome, not merely describes the outcome.
clarification: Inclusion criteria: (1) The text attributes a concrete federal benefit, project, award, grant, program, facility, designation, or policy outcome to the senator’s effort. (2) The text describes the senator’s legislative initiative as successful or as having advanced materially (passed, adopted, approved, included, confirmed, funded, designated, implemented, waived, etc.). (3) The text announces that money, resources, or official recognition has been secured and links that outcome to the senator’s announcement, request, or advocacy. (4) The text explicitly claims that the senator ‘helped secure,’ ‘worked to include,’ ‘played a key role,’ ‘delivered,’ ‘secured,’ ‘fought for and won,’ or otherwise achieved something for constituents or a policy priority. (5) The text highlights passage, adoption, or implementation of a senator-sponsored amendment, provision, or bill as a success.

positive_examples.text: I fully support the development and construction of this airport I helped secure an expedited environmental review from the federal government and facilitated the return of the project to the national priority list for federal funding.
positive_examples.explanation: The release explicitly says the senator ‘secured’ and ‘facilitated’ federal action for a local airport project. It claims concrete prior achievements in advancing a constituent project, which is credit-claiming.

positive_examples.text: Senator DeWine wrote and passed the FIRE Act (S. 1941) in 2000, establishing a grant program dedicated to providing federal assistance to local fire departments. Senator DeWine's legislation increased the federal commitment to firefighting and emergency response services.
positive_examples.explanation: The senator announces a federal grant and links the funding directly to a program he authored and passed. The release presents the senator as responsible for creating and funding the grant program that produced a local benefit.

positive_examples.text: Nebraska s Senator Ben Nelson today said he was gratified that his amendment to prevent the USDA from allowing some Japanese beef imports back into the U S until the Japanese government also allows American beef to again be imported into Japan passed on a bipartisan vote of 72 to 26.
positive_examples.explanation: The release attributes legislative success to the senator’s amendment and describes a bipartisan vote victory for a state industry. This is a clear claim of personal legislative achievement.

negative_clarification: Do not classify a text as credit-claiming when the senator: (1) only announces a bill introduction, cosponsorship, letter, request, hearing, town meeting, or ongoing effort without evidence of success; (2) criticizes the administration, another party, or Congress without claiming a personal accomplishment; (3) merely states a vote or policy position without describing it as producing a concrete achievement; (4) issues a commemorative, condolence, or celebratory statement; (5) announces a nomination, confirmation, or appointment as routine news without tying it to the senator’s own achievement; (6) describes advocacy that is still pending or unsuccessful; (7) merely reports a federal award or agency action without linking it to the senator’s effort; or (8) urges others to act while not claiming responsibility for the result.

negative_examples.text: Sen. Pete Domenici today reported that he is requesting an expedited Senate hearing on legislation he cosponsored to aid farmers and ranchers who have been impacted by the severe winter storms in New Mexico and the region.
negative_examples.explanation: The senator is requesting a hearing and urging expedited action on disaster aid legislation. The release describes advocacy that has not yet produced a completed legislative outcome, so it is not credit-claiming.

negative_examples.text: Today we remember the brave Americans who lost their lives 65 years ago during the attacks on Pearl Harbor Each year on December 7 we are reminded of the price our military men and women have paid to protect us and our freedoms.
negative_examples.explanation: The release is a commemorative statement about Pearl Harbor. It does not claim that the senator secured a benefit, passed legislation, or achieved a policy outcome.

negative_examples.text: Below is a statement from Senator John Kerry Today the plug was mercifully pulled on the ownership of U S port operations by Dubai Ports World It s been a case study in the Administration s incompetence and inattention to the fundamental issue of port security.
negative_examples.explanation: The senator criticizes the administration’s handling of the ports deal. Although the administration changed course, the senator does not claim personal responsibility for that result; the text is criticism rather than credit-claiming.
